speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To better understand your condition, have you noticed if these symptoms radiate specifically to your fingers, and can you point to the exact areas of weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with C8-T1 radiculopathy.

The patient's one-year history of burning neck/arm pain, hand paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness, combined with his age and vascular risk factors, strongly suggests cervical spondylosis with myelopathy and lower cervical radiculopathy.
